messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing intermittent dropped final chunks when the Node SDK refreshes auth during an active SSE stream. Happens in our sample chat app after ~30s of inactivity.

maria: ugh, yes saw that in staging yesterday. Stream just ends without the [DONE] event?

alex: Exactly. Client never gets the terminal `data: [DONE]` line. Server logs show the request was proxied and a 401 -> 200 refresh happened.

jon: Do you have a minimal repro? sounds like race between token refresh + connection abort.

alex: Minimal steps: 1) open streaming call, 2) wait for token auto-refresh window (we refresh when expire <10s), 3) we reauth then re-open connection, but sometimes the original SSE socket gets closed by fetch abort and some chunks are lost mid-chunk.

kevin: Can you paste the client-side fetch code? there was that old bug where abort() triggers stream parser to drop last buffered chunk.

alex: Snippet: ```js
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch(url, { headers, signal: controller.signal })
  .then(res => {
    const reader = res.body.getReader();
    // parse chunks via decoder + split by "\n\n"
  });
// token refresh path calls controller.abort() then re-auth and reconnect
```

sam: Interesting — in browsers fetch abort can leave a partially read chunk unreported. Our SSE parser assumes chunks always end on a full event boundary. If abort happens mid-event the parser drops it.

maria: Is this Node-only or repros in the browser too? We need parity across SDKs.

alex: We hit it in Node 18+ and in a headful Chrome run. But browser seemed rarer (maybe because keepalive/frame sizes differ).

jon: Logging from Node shows sequences like: `chunk1\n\ndata: partial`, then abort, then reconnect and a new stream with `data: rest\n\n[data: [DONE]]` but client missed `rest` because parser reset.

kevin: Two fixes: 1) make parser tolerant of partial events on abort (flush buffer on abort), 2) change auth flow to do graceful reconnect instead of abort mid-request. I'd vote for both.

alex: Agreed. I can open PR for the parser change in node-sdk: ensure decoder saves partial chunk and on 'close/abort' treats remaining bytes as a final fragment and attempts to parse any `data:` lines.

sam: Need to be careful — treating partial bytes as final could cause duplicate partial events if server later sends the remainder on reconnect. Must dedupe via Last-Event-ID or a request-scoped stream id.

maria: Do we emit Last-Event-ID from the server? I thought our runtime doesn't set event ids for generated tokens.

jon: We don't today. We could add a lightweight per-stream sequence header the runtime echoes back for idempotency. But that's a bigger server change. For SDK-level fix, we can: on abort, flush buffer and surface a recoverable error to caller so sample apps can re-request with resume token.

alex: For immediate mitigation, PR will: flush partial lines into an 'incomplete' event and emit an event like `__SSE_PARTIAL__` with payload. Devs can log or retry. Will also add integration test that simulates mid-chunk abort.

kevin: Add test harness that simulates: server writes `data: foo\n\n` then `data: partial` then EOF. Assert parser emits foo then emits partial-on-abort.

sam: Also update node SDK auth helper to avoid aborting active streams when token refresh is scheduled. Instead: 1) if stream age < threshold, let it finish, 2) otherwise try to refresh using a parallel short-lived token request and only force abort as last resort.

maria: We'll need parity in python SDK and browser SDKs. Can you add test cases in each repo? The tests should be small and live under `tests/streaming` so our CI can run them fast.

alex: Yep. I'll do Node PR + test. I'll add a sample-app change to show recommended pattern: on auth refresh, post a graceful `:reconnect` comment in chat UI and attempt to resume, not abrupt abort.

kevin: One more thought — our reconnect/backoff needs to preserve a per-request `stream-request-id` header so server can reconcile partials later. If we add that server-side, SDK can send last-received-offset. Will file an infra issue.

alex: Filing infra ticket now: INFRA-1223 (link will be added).

devex-bot: New PR referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/789 — parser flush on abort + tests (draft).

maria: Nice. Can you also add a short note in onboarding sample-app README about long-running streams and auth refresh behavior? New devs keep implementing naive abort-on-refresh and hit this.

alex: Will add README note + code example showing `signal` usage and `onabort` handler to flush parser and surface partials.

sam: For the browser SDK, we should avoid exposing `AbortController` to users as the primary auth knob — instead provide an sdk-managed auto-refresh that returns a `reconnect()` hook. We need design doc.

jon: I'll sketch a short ADR for SDK auth parity and streaming semantics so everyone implements same behavior across languages.

sara: Thanks for catching this, alex — saved us from a weird production bug. :raised_hands:

alex: thanks all. I'll post PR and test links when ready.

maria: follow-up: can you include a repro gif or playback if possible, makes triage faster.

alex: Will do — attaching in a follow-up message.
